name: Anti-wrinkle pillow
lead: Anti-wrinkle pillows are contoured, cut-out or cushioned pillows, and pillowcase-style products, marketed to reduce pressure and creasing of the face against the bedding during sleep. The premise is that repeated compression of the same facial areas, particularly in side and stomach sleepers, contributes to sleep lines on the forehead, cheeks and chest. Related products use silk, satin or metal-infused covers aimed at reducing friction.

Wikipedia's article on wrinkles lists habitual sleeping positions among the factors that can contribute to skin wrinkling alongside ageing processes, sun damage, weight loss and habitual facial expressions [1]. No clinical trial of anti-wrinkle pillows was found in the sources reviewed, so product claims rest on that general theory and on manufacturer descriptions.
infobox: Contoured pillow or pillowcase intended to reduce facial compression
Less facial pressure and shear; lower friction for silk-type covers

paras: Designs include pillows with cut-outs or channels intended to let the cheek or forehead rest without contact, cradle-shaped or wedge pillows that encourage back sleeping, and flat pillowcases made of silk, satin or copper-infused fabric intended to let skin glide rather than drag. Pillows in general are bedding items designed for head and neck support and comfort, in varied shapes, sizes and fillings [2].

Wikipedia describes the misrepair-accumulation theory of ageing, in which facial wrinkles develop from incorrect repair of elastic and collagen fibres that are injured by repeated extension and compression of the skin [1]. Proponents of anti-wrinkle pillows apply this idea to sleep, arguing that hours of facial compression each night add up. The sources reviewed do not report measurements linking specific pillow shapes or covers to wrinkle formation, and wrinkles are also attributed to sun damage, ageing and other factors [1].

Risks are low. Reported downsides are discomfort or disturbed sleep from an unfamiliar shape, which could offset any intended benefit, and cost. Wikipedia lists sun exposure, smoking, ageing and other factors as promoters of wrinkling [1], and treatments with evidence, such as topical retinoids, are discussed in dermatology sources [1].

Within skin-care and appearance communities, sleeping position is sometimes discussed as a cause of facial lines, with back sleeping suggested as a no-cost alternative to specialised pillows. Specialised pillows and silk cases are commonly offered at prices of roughly $40 to $100. Marketing material for these products is a main source of supporting claims; the sources reviewed contain no independent evaluation.
